observation: Founder redirect × three concept drafts: AL5 concept reshaped THREE times (MCP-Apps ui:// → rejected; declarative-config templates → rejected; code/registry/adoption → locked) over 29 min, driven by two explicit redirects. Founder called out first research pass was adoption-ergonomics not OSS-templating mechanics (shadcn/Docusaurus/Radix). When a concept probes mechanics (registry, templating, distribution), pre-research the actual mechanics before probing adoption frame.

Two live-path bugs (teamId missing on API calls) passed green tests + initial review verdict DONE; caught only by reviewer's NIT flag + builder's notice. ReviewPage defaultLoader + SettingsReviewSurfaces both missing ?teamId= query/body param → 400 → adoptions silently fell to []. Real API contract untested (URL shape, param presence, routing). Tests use fixtures; no end-to-end component→API path. Instance of CC-004 (wiring gap) at component-to-API layer.

Architecture-critique (Phase 2) caught WARN-1 before build: StripeRefundReview wrapping ReviewActionOperation would silently drop AL7 OutcomeBand if surface didn't forward status/outcome/proposedCall props. Critique found prose mismatch ('same signature as base canvas' FALSE for action_operation). Builder resolved by discriminating surface component contract per base canvas kind. Exemplary: architect-critique caught load-bearing claim with independent reads; architect fixed plan; builder implemented clean result. Protect this discipline.

Green phase was long + wide: single builder session ~3h 43m, 24 commits, 55 files, +9188 lines. Full-stack: shared types, web (review/ + settings/), db (schema + migration + routes), server routes, eslint-plugin-design rule. Scope wide but sustainable (concept locked 5h before green; no timeouts; no rework). L-class workpackage by breadth not depth. Builder had maximal context from extended concept lock. Pattern healthy.

Pipeline ran on concept branch (concept/AL5-tool-tailored-canvases, PR #361) rather than origin/main; concept not merged first. Non-standard workflow but smooth practicality (no friction reported). Branch was based on origin/main; all phases (design/architecture/build) happened on branch. Unclear if this is (a) one-off due to contentious concept (three redirects) or (b) new pattern for foundational concepts. Document decision rule: when does a pipeline stack on non-main?

AL5 first review-surface WP revealed canvas prop-contract asymmetries: ReviewActionOperation (proof vehicle) wider than ReviewCanvasComponent (accepts AL7 props: status/outcome/proposedCall). Original architecture promised 'same signature' (FALSE). Builder resolved by discriminating registry entry per base canvas kind. Cost: registry type is discriminated union, not uniform component type. Future slot-wiring on other 8 canvases will encounter similar asymmetries. Before fast-follow, enumerate each canvas's extra props beyond ReviewCanvasProps.

All 5 ACs + validation scenarios shipped with tests exercising real paths (not mocks). Sanity-break tests: resolveSurface floor-fallback went RED on revert; adoption unique index went RED on revert; AC5 lint rule went RED on neuter. Load-bearing invariants (no-auto-apply via unique index, floor-fallback via error boundary, AC5 lint) tested against real code. Exemplary for AC completeness + test quality. Preserve sanity-break discipline.

Docs phase retired plan artifacts (concept.md, architecture.md, design/*.md, review.md, *-critique.md; 1013 lines) to git history; committed ground-truth docs: docs/guides/developer/review-surfaces.md (208 lines), docs/guides/user/review-surfaces.md (70 lines), updated docs/human-interface-layer/review-primitive.md. Correct /write-docs workflow. Ground-truth docs captured essence (slot policy table, component contract, manifest, layering modes). No loss of context.
